result.killer: None found. Gaps not settled: the FOO electronic STR/CTR reporting channel, local consultancies selling templates (I found none with prices), and the number of obliged entities.
result.reason: I found nothing that kills it. Bosnian, Serbian and Croatian searches turned up no local or regional AML software, model-act generator or free state tool for small non-financial obliged entities. Asseco's AML product is built for banks, and UK tools (FigsFlow, SmartSearch) have no BiH forms. Enforcement is real: in January 2026 the RS Inspectorate gave randomly chosen accountants, bookkeepers and tax advisers 10 days to submit internal acts, a 13-item questionnaire and a checklist, with fines up to 200,000 KM. That burden on sole traders drew public complaints. RS notaries also got risk-assessment guidelines in January 2026. Against it: BiH is a small market, buyers are price-sensitive, and the core need is a one-off document set that consultants can sell. Not checked: whether the FOO has an electronic reporting portal, and how many entities there are.

Narcotics: importers file quarterly reports to ALMBiH (Law 8/2006). Nov 2025 draft moves cannabis to a strictly controlled table (not confirmed adopted). No pharmacy-level narcotics/precursor register duty found.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Found only the Brcko District law on agencies for securing persons and property and private detectives (Sl. glasnik BD 27/2004, am. 15/2005, 37/2005) and old FBiH/RS items. No 2024-2026 amendment or reporting duty found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: No current FBiH rules on construction diary/book or contractor licensing surfaced; FBiH spatial planning law amendments with e-permits were only drafts (2022-2023 news), status unknown. Kanton Sarajevo spatial law (Apr 2025) is cantonal. Nothing usable.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: State-level AML/CFT Law, Sl. glasnik BiH 13/2024 (19 Feb 2024); real estate agents/brokers, notaries, lawyers and accountants are obliged entities (authorised person + deputy, risk assessment, internal procedures, 5-year records). A guide for real estate dealers was published on fuzip.gov.ba in March 2026 (partly read from PDF: mentions transactions above 30,000 KM and cash limits; exact thresholds unverified). Implementing rulebook adopted by the Council of Ministers (paragraf.ba 5 Jan 2026). FATF/MONEYVAL pressure: 1-year observation period from Feb 2025, grey-list risk. No local AML software vendor found. See C1.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: RS: central electronic guest/tourist registration system (eTurizam, eturizam.vladars.rs) in use from 1 Jan 2026; tourist tax law amended 1 Jan 2025 (1.5-3 KM, private accommodation now covered). FBiH: cantonal e-registration system prijava.ba, presented Oct 2025, now covering all ten cantons (Feb 2026 report), mandatory in Herzegovina-Neretva Canton. Free state systems cover the core duty. See C8 (rejected). FBiH tourist tax law revision only at pre-draft stage (2025).

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Wood EUDR digital traceability: TI BiH (Feb 2026) warns BiH wood products cannot cross the border without EUDR-aligned traceability (known K02). BiH has EU approval for fish, honey, hides, sugar exports (old EEAS source); no current establishment list or exporter register found. Nothing new beyond K02.

coverage.category: 31. Agricultural holding register (RPG) and farm subsidy applications
coverage.found: FBiH Government adopted the 2026 agricultural support program in late April 2026 worth 190 million KM (paragraf.ba 27 Apr 2026); draft program (fmpvs.gov.ba, Feb 2026) requires entry in the Register of Agricultural Holdings / Register of Clients, beekeepers also in the Beekeepers' Register. RS 2026 program not found. See C4.

coverage.category: 32. Renewable energy: prosumers and solar installers (FBiH/RS)
coverage.found: FBiH prosumer category since 2023; installation by an authorised installer; OIEiEK operator public call for household prosumer subsidies (4 million KM, 50-100% co-financing, reported 2 Oct 2026); FBiH renewables law draft with auctions 2025-2030. RS VAT mismatch reported 2024. Installer authorisation rules and energy certificate duty not found. See C5.

coverage.category: 33. FBiH Law on Fiscalization of Transactions and B2B/B2C/B2G e-invoicing
coverage.found: Law published Sl. novine FBiH 9/2026 (4 Feb 2026); full application by 31 Aug 2027; ESET software model with real-time reporting; Tax Administration FBiH RFI May 2026, by-laws due about Aug 2026. Same duty and buyer group as K06/K03/K10. No RS e-invoicing duty found. See C9 (known).

coverage.category: 34. Packaging waste and extended producer responsibility (FBiH)
coverage.found: FBiH Rulebook on packaging and packaging waste (Sl. novine FBiH 88/2011, 28/2013, 103/2016, 84/2017; a 2016 notice says an earlier version ceased to apply, so current text unclear). Producers, importers, fillers, distributors can transfer duties by contract to an authorised operator (Ekopak named as first operator). Producer-level reporting forms/deadlines not found. See C6 (unverified).

coverage.category: 35. Employment of persons with disabilities: quota and special contribution (FBiH)
coverage.found: FBiH draft law on professional rehabilitation and employment of persons with disabilities (parliament, Mar 2025) would strengthen the Fund, tighten collection of the special contribution from all legal entities and add an employer self-service app. Adoption not confirmed. See C7.

coverage.category: 36. Narcotics list changes and medical cannabis (state level)
coverage.found: Nov 2025 draft amendment to the list of narcotics, psychotropic substances and precursors would move cannabis to the strictly controlled table; initiative by Ministry of Civil Affairs; adoption not confirmed. No licensing regime for growers found. See C12 (unverified).

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No household-employer register or dedicated regime found in FBiH, RS or Brcko. General rules apply: FBiH employers (natural persons included) file JS3100 with the Porezna uprava FBiH (e-filing allowed); RS Zakon o radu covers natural-person employers, and RS tax law requires registration the day before work starts. RFE/UN Women piece (slobodnaevropa.org/a/zene-bih-zaposlenje-domacinstva/31494224.html) says much household and elder care is in the grey zone; contributions are about 70% of net pay; reform only proposed. New lead found: RS Zakon o radnom angažovanju na sezonskim i drugim poslovima privremenog karaktera (passed by urgent procedure, late Dec 2025, per paragraf.ba) makes natural persons (farm households) register helpers with Poreska uprava RS before work, pay contributions and issue a work-engagement confirmation; reported fine 1,500 KM. Law text, effective date and portal not seen. Nothing found for Brcko or for FBiH carer rules. No software competitor found.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water rules are cantonal in FBiH and entity-level in RS; there is no single federal rule. Sarajevo Canton Zakon o vodama (SN KS 44/22) defines local (mjesni) waterworks as user-built systems for up to 50 residents. The municipality must hand municipal systems to a registered utility within 12 months and operators must send source, user-count and treatment data to the public health institute, municipality and canton ministry. Central Bosnia Canton has utilities managing local systems with 500+ residents with municipal consent; a Donji Vakuf court dispute shows ownership conflict with Mjesna zajednica. The drinking-water regulation sets monitoring frequencies and allows exemptions below 50 consumers or 10 m3/day. Rural water often fails microbiology tests (Krivoglavci, Vogosca). Rules are fragmented by canton and the buyer is mostly volunteer local committees with little money to pay. RS water law and Brcko not found. Nothing strong beyond a weak lead.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Found three duties. (1) BiH-level Pravilnik o posebnim uslovima evidentiranja i obiljezavanja brasna (Vijece ministara, 29.12.2005; text on uino.gov.ba): every first placer of flour (mill, custom-milling owner, trader, importer, exporter) must stick state evidence stamps on packs, apply to MVTEO on form A1 at least 30 days before delivery, keep an issued/used stamp ledger (A3), and keep monthly records of grain milled and flour produced, split own versus custom milling by owner (Art. 11). Current status in 2026 not confirmed; Zitounija (Serbia) called the stamps a non-tariff barrier. (2) FBiH Pravilnik o minimalnim uvjetima za skladistenje zitarica (SN FBiH 2/13): legal entities storing grain must be in the Registar skladista zitarica kept by the cantonal ministry; quality records required. Legal persons only. (3) FBiH draft Pravilnik o parametrima kvalitete i klasama psenice u otkupu (public consultation Feb 2026, fmpvs.gov.ba): buyers need proof of origin from farmers and calibrated moisture and protein meters; adoption not confirmed. Fitosanitarni registar (Uprava BiH za zastitu zdravlja bilja) covers importers and distributors of plants and plant products; whether it covers grain or coffee traders was not confirmed. RS grain buyer or warehouse rules not found. No software for mills or flour stamps found.

result.competitor: No product built for association filings was found in two Bosnian-language searches. Accountants and bookkeeping firms do this as a routine service. Local accounting packages (for example Pantheon or Minimax) were named only from general knowledge in a search summary and were not checked to see whether they support NPO forms. Whether FIA filing is electronic, and what its processing fee is, was not verified; a unija.com page mentions a processing fee and a CD submission.
result.duty: Annual financial statements to FIA by 28 Feb for all legal entities including associations and foundations (Zakon o računovodstvu i reviziji FBiH, Sl. novine FBiH 15/2021). Enforced in 2026: in May 2026 the Tax Administration issued misdemeanour orders to 125 entities that didn't file for 2025. Fines of 5,000-15,000 KM per entity and 500-3,000 KM per responsible person come from a 2019 source, so 2021-law amounts are unverified. Half-year reports apply mainly to companies; only 45 associations filed one for H1 2019. Rulebook 81/21 not verified. RS (APIF) and Brcko rules not reached.
result.market: 9,209 associations and foundations were registered in FBiH at the end of 2018, according to an FIA publication; the number was falling (9,821 in 2017). 2,811 associations did not file for 2018, which points to a large dormant or non-compliant group. One undated media estimate puts NGOs across BiH at about 12,000, with few of them active.
result.reason: The duty is real. Profit and non-profit legal entities in FBiH, associations included, must file annual financial statements with FIA by 28 February under the FBiH Accounting and Auditing Law (Sl. novine FBiH 15/2021). In May 2026 the Tax Administration fined 125 non-filers for 2025, so enforcement is current. Fines were 5,000-15,000 KM per entity plus 500-3,000 KM for the responsible person in 2019; current amounts are unverified. Half-year filing hardly matters: only 45 associations filed in H1 2019. About 9,200 associations are registered, but 2,811 didn't file for 2018, which suggests many are dormant. No dedicated product turned up, though local accountants and their software already handle this cheaply. Buyers are poor, filing is once a year, and it's hard to stand out.

result.market: FBiH has 135 registered real estate agencies with 177 certified agents (Federal Ministry of Trade register, as quoted by prostor.ba, undated). Around 2022 the FBiH Chamber estimated about 150 legal brokers and many unregistered ones. I found no count of accounting or bookkeeping firms, or of RS and Brcko agencies. Bookkeeping agencies are likely the bigger segment, plausibly low thousands nationwide, but this is unverified. Auditors, gambling operators and dealers in vehicles and precious goods are also obliged entities and could be added.
result.reason: The duty is real and being enforced now. The state AML/CFT law (Sl. glasnik BiH 13/2024) Art. 5 lists bookkeeping, accounting and tax firms, auditors, real estate intermediaries, lawyers and notaries as obliged entities. They must keep a documented risk assessment updated at least yearly and sent to the supervisor (Art. 10), keep internal procedures, appoint an authorised person and deputy, run client ID checks and report to the FIU. The implementing rulebook was published in Feb 2026 and gave 90 days to align. FUZIP market inspectors began special AML checks on 28 Sep 2026, running to end-2026, with fines of 5,000-200,000 KM. I found no local or regional SMB AML tool, only UK tools (Credas, Thirdfort, FigsFlow, Xama) and Asseco's bank-grade system. The market is small: 135 agencies in FBiH, and accountant counts were not found.

result.competitor: None found in one local-language search (software, app, evidence, lift, upravnik). Inspection bodies and lift service firms do the inspections. Search was shallow.
result.duty: Lift owner must ensure a regular technical inspection at least once a year (Naredba o sigurnosti liftova, Sl. glasnik BiH 99/12, art. 24). Penalties were not found.
result.market: Not quantified. No count of buildings with lifts or of upravnici was found.
result.reason: The duty is real. Art. 24 of the Naredba o sigurnosti liftova (Sl. glasnik BiH 99/12) requires the owner to ensure a technical inspection at least once a year. In 2019 the Sarajevo canton found lifts in service without an inspection and warned building managers. Not checked: the fine amounts, and whether the Naredba is still in force unchanged; Republika Srpska has its own Pravilnik (Sl. glasnik RS 105/2024). I found no dedicated lift-inspection scheduling software, but I ran only one competitor search. The task is a single annual date per lift. That is a thin product, and buyers are mostly unpaid owners' boards, so willingness to pay is low. The market is fragmented across entities and cantons, and I found no lift or building count. Lift service firms could add reminders at little cost. Score 3.

The FBiH rulebook is not just a draft. A search summary says it was published in Sl. novine FBiH 58/2024 (26 July 2024) and amended in Sl. novine FBiH 36/2026 (May 2026). It covers small-business waste operators outside environmental-permit scope: permits, collection and storage, and a waste management elaborate. I could not read the PDF, so frequency, penalties and the information-system duties are unverified. I found no BiH-specific software or state portal, but only two searches were run, so absence of competition is weak evidence. Market size is unknown and the segment is informal and fragmented. Entity-level split (RS differs) and low willingness to pay limit the score. The permit is mostly one-off, not recurring.

The EU rule is real and in force since 1 July 2026: G2V2 is required on vehicles of 2.5-3.5 t in international carriage or cabotage for hire or reward (secondary sources only). BiH is not an EU member. A search summary cited a Paragraf.ba report that Serbian-registered vans have no duty because AETR has not been amended. That would likely apply to BiH too, but I did not read that article, and the Paragraf page I fetched does not mention AETR or registration country. I found no BiH-specific law, penalty or vendor search results. Market size is unknown. Demand is mostly an installation purchase from certified workshops, not recurring software. Frotcom and similar fleet vendors cover tacho downloads. Weak SaaS case.

The duty is real, but it is not a recurring software workflow. Paragraf.ba (11 Jul 2025) confirms the FBiH inspectorate checked BAS EN 16942 dispenser labelling and the prescribed fuel-movement documentation from Jul to Oct 2025. The article names no penalties, and the campaign has ended. Labelling is a one-off physical task. Fuel-movement documents are probably handled by suppliers and ERP or POS vendors. I could not confirm the OPC/OPM filing channel (eopc.fmt.gov.ba) or the full law text. No station-software competitor turned up, but the search was thin. The 719-station market is tiny, and stations will likely buy fiscalization (ESET) software instead, under the new FBiH Fiscalization Law (Sl. novine 9/2026).

The duty is real. The FBiH 2026 support programme (190M KM, Sl. novine FBiH 6/26, adopted 23.04.2026) requires entry in the Register of Agricultural Holdings/Register of Clients. The register data has an annual update deadline, normally 31 March, extended in 2024 and 2025. But the FBiH ministry says the whole process is already electronic, from application to payment, with a Farmer web portal and a ministry application for processing payments. Applications are filed through municipal and ministry channels, and extension services and cooperatives already help with the paperwork. Farms are small, so willingness to pay is low. A private packager would sit on top of state systems, with no mandatory-software hook. Counts of farms and beekeepers, and competing private tools, were not checked.

Only one source, a Paragraf.ba news report of 30 Dec 2025, says the RS assembly passed the law under urgent procedure. It reports a 1,500 KM fine and pre-work registration of helpers with Poreska uprava RS, but this is an accountant's reading. It gives no effective date. My searches found no official text, Sl. glasnik RS entry, form or portal, and no vendor. The Tax Administration said inspectors won't check private homes, so enforcement is weak. The likely channel is a free state e-service, as in Serbia. Households register a few times a year, so willingness to pay is low and distribution to scattered farmers is hard. Law text, effective date and portal are all unconfirmed.
